brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.evidence: Spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 (addSpike at junction of cells (0,0),(0,1),(1,0)). Drawer: notch drawer frame notch:0#1,1#notch2 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) at cell (1,1), level 0.

requirements.requirement: Both at the very same corner of the same cell
requirements.evidence: The spike sits at the vertex shared by cells (0,0),(0,1),(1,0). Cell (1,1) is the cell across the (0,1)/(1,0) edge, so it contains that same vertex; the drawer frame sits in (1,1) and touches the spike there. I read 'the same corner of the same cell' as this shared vertex, since the spike's vertex is not a corner of any empty cell other than (1,1). The drawer is a frame filling cell (1,1), not a standalone drawer at the vertex.
Spike and notch frame share the vertex (configurator accepted both; check_build meshClash clear, no issues).

finish.summary: Built a small structure: full bases at (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), a half-e base at (-1,0), with a spike at the junction of the first three cells and a notch drawer frame in cell (1,1) that shares that corner. The half-e base was added only to test drawer offers and is not needed for the request. House rules applied: caps on open faces and joints locked. check_build is clean with meshClash clear. Nothing dressed. Caveat: the drawer is a notch frame in a cell, not a drawer placed at a bare point, and I took 'same corner of the same cell' to mean the shared vertex.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
